{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

**Without labels, SFT on the 2B's own answers (B) took Qwen3.5-0.8B from
`{python} h["before"]` to `{python} h["after"]` exact match on xLAM test-clean, past its teacher's
`{python} h["teacher"]` and `{python} h["share_of_a"]` of what gold labels gain, in
`{python} h["gpu_hours"]` GPU-hours on one 12 GB card.** On-policy distillation (D), logit
distillation (C) and grounded B can't be separated from it on test-clean. D leads B's selected
checkpoint on unseen tools, at `{python} f"{d_cost / b_cost:.1f}"`× the cost; with one seed, that
can't be told apart from more training.

## Serving and the model

In vLLM on the same card, the 0.8B answers **`{python} serve["one_at_a_time"]` faster** than the 2B
one request at a time, and serves **`{python} serve["batched"]` cheaper** with every test-clean
prompt batched: the prompts are long and the answers short, so batching narrows the gap.

The headline model is B at step `{python} story.facts("B")["step"]`, a LoRA adapter on the 0.8B.
Its own serving run and its release on the Hugging Face Hub are
[#96](https://github.com/joaomigueloliveira/qwen-function-calling-distillation/issues/96).
